abstract: A 30-yr-old woman with previously resected papillary thyroid carcinoma was found to have a pelvic lesion which concentrated radioiodine. By performing simultaneous 131I whole-body and 99mTc-methylene diphosphonate bone scans, we found the lesion to be in soft tissue between the sacrum and bladder. Radioiodine therapy was postponed so that the lesion, a benign teratoma of the rectal wall, could be surgically removed. Prior to laparotomy, the patient received a second tracer dose of 131I so that the lesion could be located at surgery with a hand-held gamma detector. A postoperative whole-body 131I scan confirmed that the lesion had been removed, thus reducing the absorbed radiation that would have been received by the ovaries during radioiodine therapy. Although the lesion contained both thyroid and gastric epithelium, accumulated 131I was limited to the area with thyroid follicles.
abstract_ja: 以前に切除された乳頭状甲状腺癌を有する30歳の女性が、放射性ヨウ素を集積する骨盤内病変を認めた。131Iの全身スキャンと99mTcメチレンジホスホネート骨シンチグラフィーを同時に行い、病変は仙骨と膀胱の間の軟部組織にあることがわかった。放射性ヨウ素治療は、この病変が良性の直腸壁奇形腫であったため延期され、外科的に摘出された。開腹術の前に、手持ちのガンマ検出器で手術中に病変を同定できるよう、追加の131I追跡子用量を投与した。術後の131I全身スキャンで病変が摘除されたことが確認され、放射性ヨウ素治療による卵巣への被曝線量を減らすことができた。この病変には甲状腺と胃の上皮が含まれていたが、集積した131Iは甲状腺濾胞のある領域に限られていた。
